title: hw_forge interface definition
description: One standardized connector interface, as kicad_ifcheck.py checks it. A definition lives in scripts/interfaces/<id>.json or PROJECT/interfaces/<id>.json, or as a fenced ```json block inside kb/interfaces/<card>.md or PROJECT/kb/interfaces/<card>.md whose object carries "schema": "hw_forge.interface". The first definition of an id wins, in that order: shipped, knowledge-base roots, project. Rule ids are transcribed from skills/hw-design/references/interfaces.md, which is the human-readable source; this file is the machine-readable form of those tables. Version 1: add keys, never rename or re-mean one.

id.description: The value design.py's PARTS[ref].interface names, e.g. usb-c-device. Lowercase; a role after a colon (jst-ph-2:battery) is part of an alias, not of a base id.

reference.description: Where the rules are argued, with section, e.g. references/interfaces.md §1.

sources.description: Standards and datasheets the numbers come from, as cited in the reference.

aliases.description: Other interface strings this definition answers, e.g. jst-ph-2:battery. An exact id match always wins over an alias.

ground_pattern.description: Regex (Python re, matched case-insensitively against the net name with any leading '/' removed) that identifies a ground net. Default: ^(gnd|vss|0v|agnd|dgnd|pgnd|gnd_.*|.*_gnd)$

roles.description: Role name -> how a connector pin is recognised as that role. A pin matches by pad number or by symbol pin name (the netlist's pinfunction). design.py PARTS[ref].pin_map {role: [pins]} replaces `pins` for one part, which is how a pigtail's vendor-specific polarity is stated.

required.description: The part must have at least one pin in this role, and that pin must be on a net with another node.

id.description: Rule id from the reference's table, e.g. UC-DEV-01.

kind.description: connected: every pin of `roles` sits on a net with another node. same_net: all pins of each role in `roles` share one net. distinct_nets: the roles in `roles` are on pairwise different nets. net_pattern / net_not_pattern: the role's net does / does not match `pattern` ("ground" means ground_pattern). passive_to: for each role in `roles`, exactly `count` parts whose ref prefix is in `prefixes` have one pin on the role's net and another on `to_role`'s net (or a ground net when to_role is "ground"), with value inside value_ohms/value_farads x (1 +/- tolerance). no_passive_to: no such part exists. part_on_net: at least one such part exists for each role, any value. part_to_net: for each role in `roles`, parts whose ref prefix is in `prefixes` with one pin on the role's net and another on a net that is neither ground nor any role's net, narrowed by `to_net` when given (an electret load resistor to a bias rail, a series build-out resistor); exactly `count` when given, else at least one, each inside value_ohms/value_farads x (1 +/- tolerance) when given. manual: a review step with no script; reported as MANUAL, never PASS.

to_net.description: part_to_net only: regex (Python re, case-insensitive, searched in the net name with any sheet path removed) naming the far net. Ground nets and role nets never match.

prefixes.description: Reference prefixes a passive kind counts. Absent: passives only (R, C, L, D, FB). Do-not-populate parts never count.

count.description: Exact number of parts; 0 means none may exist. Passive kinds only. Each part counts once.

text.description: The rule sentence from the reference table.

mating.description: Placement rules checked against the fit contract (kicad_geom.py --contract) when kicad_ifcheck.py is given --board.

direction_required.description: PARTS[ref].mating_direction (or the footprint field of that name) must be declared.

edge_required.description: The mating face must point out through a board edge (contract mating.kind == edge, verdict PASS), unless PARTS[ref].access is internal and internal_allowed is true.

max_inset_mm.description: Largest distance the mating face may sit inboard of its edge.

max_overhang_mm.description: Largest distance the body may overhang the edge before the overhang is reported.
